result.title: HOPD: Historical On-Policy Distillation for SAR MLLM Continual Learning
result.summary: Continual SAR interpretation requires multimodal large language models to learn incoming sources while retaining earlier task abilities. This is difficult when acquisition and geographic shifts alter visual evidence, regionally concentrated categories bias answers, and historical images are scarce. We address this problem with Historical On-Policy Distillation (HOPD), which reuses source-acquisition LoRA states as persistent teachers for one evolving student. Archiving each state before consolidation preserves a stable source reference. The teachers supervise student-generated prefixes, transferring historical behavior to the student's changing generation contexts. To enrich sparse replay, original-view teachers guide augmented historical student views while preserving spatial coordinates. This knowledge is consolidated into a single deployed adapter that requires no source identity. On SARVQA-CL, our source-incremental evaluation protocol, HOPD achieves the highest final mean score of 54.51 among the compared methods, exceeding the strongest baseline by 2.96 points. It also improves the final source-macro score in every evaluated task over shared-memory Replay-SFT, with gains across source orders. These results support source-acquisition history as supervision for retaining earlier task performance during continual SAR adaptation. Code and data: https://github.com/zcablii/HOPD.

AI.brief_summary: 面向 SAR 多模态大模型持续学习，将各源采集阶段的 LoRA 状态归档为持续教师，对学生自生成前缀做 on-policy 蒸馏，并用原始视角教师指导增强后的历史视图，最终合并为单一适配器。
AI.relevance_reason: 教师监督学生自生成前缀的 on-policy 蒸馏可供核查 LVR 轨迹训练中的监督信号与贡献分配问题；但该文针对灾难性遗忘与 SAR 域偏移，未涉及内部视觉状态或推理期 latent 生成，需判断其「自生成前缀」与 latent 推理轨迹是否有实质可比性。
